newsitem.title: JAPAN: General Sekiyu to set up electricity joint venture.
newsitem.headline: General Sekiyu to set up electricity joint venture.

text.p: Oil refiner General Sekiyu KK said on Friday that it would set up a joint venture with trading house Mitsui & Co Ltd to handle its electricity wholesaling.
The refiner, owned 49 percent by Exxon Corp of the United States, plans to supply Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) with 547,500 kilowatts of power for 15 years from June 2001.
General Sekiyu did not give details of the venture with Mitsui.
TEPCO on Thursday said it had selected eight electricity suppliers in its first-ever power buying tender.
Apart from General Sekiyu, the winners included Nippon Petroleum Refining Co Ltd, a subsidiary of Nippon Oil Co Ltd and Showa Denko KK.
General Sekiyu plans to invest a total of 70 billion yen to build power generating facilities in Kawasaki, south of Tokyo, to be fired by residual fuel oil.
Until deregulation last December, Japan's electricity industry was monopolised by 10 major power firms. Now the business is open to independent power producers.
